correctness.rationale: For a traceless strictly positive-off-diagonal real 2×2 generator part, its square is (d²+pq)I. The centered propagator product has determinant one and half-trace C=cosh(uT)cosh(vT)+h sinh(uT)sinh(vT), with u=aφ, v=b(1−φ). Strict positivity gives a simple pair of positive eigenvalues, and h>−1 follows from ab>|d_A d_B| and the positive off-diagonal cross-terms. Writing C as the affine combination of cosh(T√x) at x=(u+v)² and x=(u−v)² with weight (1+h)/2 shows strict Jensen for h<1 and strict secant extrapolation for h>1; the averaged eigenvalue uses that same affine combination in x before applying cosh. Thus the exact sign and equality case hold. Computing the T⁴ discrepancy between C and cosh(qT) gives (1−h²)u²v²T⁴/6; dividing by the leading arcosh derivative denominator qT and by T yields the stated quadratic correction. The coefficient of the fastest cosh is positive, so the long-period limit is the duty-weighted average of the phase exponents. The witness gives a²=5/4, b²=7 and ab h=3; its two endpoint exponents have opposite signs by the stated rational square comparisons. For the other sign one can take equal positive switching rates with dose-dependent sensitive growth and fixed tolerant growth: the symmetric traceless parts are nonparallel, giving h<1. The saturating-law witness lies in the frozen assumptions, which do not require the tolerant growth rate to exceed the active one under the selected dose.

evidence: Using the dyadic comparison above, the entire chain Λ(T/2^j) is strictly ordered with common sign det[A,B], or constant when the determinant vanishes. The first-order expansion of the two-phase product as T/2^j→0 gives its limit α(φA+(1−φ)B). Traceless anticommutation A₀B₀+B₀A₀=2ab hI gives [A,B]²=4a²b²(h²−1)I, so det[A,B]=4a²b²(1−h²). For h>−1 this has sign 1−h. The four-pulse example also expressly shows that a common scalar shift can place zero between strictly ordered stability exponents.

This uses no hypothesis outside the frozen matrix class, even if the four-pulse application is narrower. evidence: Greene's unrestricted deterministic identity is tr(X²Y²)−tr((XY)²)=det[X,Y]. The four-pulse record explicitly compares largest eigenvalues at a common positive determinant and replaces the exponential commutator by a positive scalar times the generator commutator.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Take X=exp(φTA/2), Y=exp((1−φ)TB/2). The grouped product X²Y² is one period T; (XY)² gives the same-duration rate Λ(T/2). The two products have identical positive determinants, positive entries, and Perron eigenvalues strictly ordered by trace. Because each phase exponential is cI+sM with s>0, the sign of Λ(T)−Λ(T/2) is exactly sign det[A,B]. This is a strict fixed-duty comparison whenever the determinant is nonzero, valid for every T.
